newsitem.title: USA: Jordan's Hussein resting after prostate surgery.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Hussein resting after prostate surgery.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein was resting comfortably on Saturday after a one-hour operation to correct a benign enlargement of the prostate gland, his physician said in a statement.

No evidence of cancer was found and the operation was not related to surgery the king underwent in August 1992 for cancer, according to a statement from King Hussein's physician, released by the Mayo Clinic on Saturday.

According to Dr. Samir Farraj, who participated in the surgery with a Mayo surgeon, the king was awake during the operation and went through the operation "without problems or discomfort of any kind."

King Hussein is expected to remain at Rochester Methodist Hospital for three to five days and doctors are expected to recommend restricted physical activity for three to four weeks, according to the statement from Farraj.

Hussein is expected to receive at least one visitor on Sunday -- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who plans to visit the king in the afternoon before a White House meeting with (U.S.) President Bill Clinton on Monday.

The procedure King Hussein underwent on Saturday, a transurethral resection of the prostate, is the surgical procedure most often chosen by urologists to decrease the size of an enlarged prostate, according to the statement. The procedure usually relieves all of the symptoms caused by the enlarged gland, which include obstruction of the flow of urine.
